H1_MEIS1_CIRCADIAN.note: the title names 'MEIS1 risk variation' but the chain starts at MEIS1; sign neg because H1.1 makes MEIS1 required for the normal cycle and the title has the risk variation act by disrupting it. The mechanism text says the direction of MEIS1 expression change is not established

H2_BTBD9_SLEEP_SENSORY.note: the title names 'BTBD9 risk variation' but the chain starts at 'BTBD9 dysfunction' (loss of function, so neg); the mechanism says the direction of the risk allele is unresolved. The chain also concludes periodic limb movements; RLS is the run's disease

H3_PTPRD_MOTOR_CIRCUIT.note: the title names 'PTPRD risk variation' but the chain starts at 'PTPRD dysfunction' (neg); the mechanism only says the risk allele 'changes PTPRD activity'

H4_ACO1_IRON_MODIFIER.note: title 'ACO1 dysfunction may modify RLS'; aspect risk because the chain ends at 'RLS susceptibility', though the mechanism calls it a modifier hypothesis

findings.detail: H1.1 ends at 'normal circadian sleep/wake cycle' (kind process), H1.2 starts at 'disrupted circadian sleep/wake cycle' (kind phenotype); same node in opposite states, curated as one node, HP:0006979 'Sleep-wake cycle disturbance' (the human match of MP:0020478, which the run's mechanism names)

every step that reaches RLS cites only GWAS variant-RLS association rows or GWAS abstracts, none of which mention the step's subject (circadian cycle, sensory circuit, motor-circuit disinhibition); the steps' own notes concede this
H1, H2 and H3 cite human GWAS risk alleles but no chain has a variant-to-gene step, so the only human evidence in the run cannot enter any arm

H1-H3 chains assert loss of gene function ('BTBD9 dysfunction', 'PTPRD dysfunction', 'MEIS1 required for'), while their mechanisms say the risk allele's direction is unresolved and no cited record gives a risk allele's effect on expression or function

H2.1 and H2.2 are parallel branches from 'BTBD9 dysfunction' ending at abnormal somatosensory morphology/electrophysiology and abnormal sleep behaviour; H2.3 starts at 'sleep-dependent sensory-circuit dysfunction' (abnormal central sensory function during sleep), which neither reaches

the sleep phenotype is from a Purkinje-cell (Pcp2-cre) conditional knockout and the somatosensory cortex phenotype from a forebrain (Emx1-cre) one; no cited record shows a somatosensory circuit with a sleep phenotype, as the mechanism proposes
the electrophysiology record is a whole-body Btbd9 tm1d knockout with 'abnormal nervous system electrophysiology' and no site; the run relabels it 'somatosensory-circuit electrophysiology'

PMID:17634447, which the run cites at H2.3, finds the BTBD9 variant associated with periodic limb movements without RLS and 'the absence of such an association for RLS without periodic limb movements', calling it a determinant of PLMS; the run lumps 'RLS and periodic limb movements' and builds a sensory mechanism without noting this
H3.1 ends at 'impaired motor function' (a deficit), H3.2 starts at 'motor-circuit disinhibition' (excess activity); different nodes, arguably opposite in direction, and no step links them
the cited record shows impaired swimming in Ptprd-null mice; the run generalises it to 'impaired motor function' (kept, as swimming is a motor function, but the run itself calls it nonspecific)

H4.1 ends at 'abnormal iron homeostasis' (a whole-body Aco1 knockout record), H4.2 starts at 'abnormal neural iron homeostasis'; the falsification (perturb ACO1 in neural cells while controlling systemic iron, measure brain iron) makes 'neural' the point, so they are different nodes and H4 has no route

the step from iron homeostasis to RLS cites nothing, although PMID:17634447 (cited at H2.3) says iron depletion 'has been associated with the pathogenesis of RLS' (background, association only, so it would not have been kept)
PMID:17634447 reports serum ferritin decreased 13% per BTBD9 at-risk allele, an iron link the run uses in neither H2 nor the iron hypothesis H4
PMID:17637780 also reports the MEIS1 association and says MEIS1 is implicated in limb development (a developmental mechanism), but the run cites it only for BTBD9 at H2.3

rs1820989 is intergenic (nearest LINC01812, FBXL12P1; author-reported MEIS1, C1D, APLF), 1.3 Mb from rs113851554, yet the mechanism says RLS variants 'map very strongly to MEIS1'; rs61192259 is also author-reported for GLO1

confidence 'high' and support 'grounded', but only H1.1 is stated by a citation (one mouse MGI annotation); H1.2, the link to RLS, cites only GWAS rows that do not mention the circadian cycle, so the arm's belief is 0
confidence 'high', but only the mouse knockout-to-phenotype steps H2.1 (morphology) and H2.2 are supported; the link to RLS is uncited in substance and disconnected from them
confidence 'medium' on one mouse impaired-swimming annotation and GWAS rows that do not state the motor-circuit step; no route from PTPRD to RLS
H1 and H3 falsifications describe engineering or introducing the risk haplotype but label the perturbation action 'restore'
GLIPR1 and GABARAPL2 get no hypothesis (the run lists them as unexplained); ACO1 gets one despite no GWAS support

the run's contradicting citation (no GWAS Catalog ACO1-RLS association) bears on the hypothesis's gene-to-disease claim, which no step states, so it can only be excluded; it is also a catalogue absence, not a tested null, and the run fairly kept confidence low
BLN:MotorCircuitDisinhibition: no ontology term for reduced inhibition in motor circuits (HP:0000734 'Disinhibition' is behavioural)

'required_for normal X' maps to an effect on process X, and an MGI 'abnormal X' knockout annotation is then no_direction; the audit read 'required for normal X' as 'losing the gene gives abnormal X' (MEIS1 →− HP:0006979), as another RLS curation did, which keeps exactly the record that states it; the guide should say which

'disrupted X' is in neither the loss-of-function list (invert) nor the undirected list (abnormal-X phenotype); the curator read it as loss of function, the audit as undirected, since a disrupted cycle is abnormal, not reduced, and the run's mechanism calls it 'an abnormal circadian sleep/wake cycle'

no rule for HP versus MP when a human-gene step's phenotype comes from a mouse annotation; HP used where an exact equivalent exists (HP:0006979, HP:0001311, HP:0011031), MP otherwise (MP:0000860, MP:0011396)
HP:0004302 'Functional motor deficit' has no definition and its synonyms show as '\1' in the corpus, so the grounding of 'impaired motor function' could not be checked against a definition

an MGI annotation counts as curatedDb whatever the allele: a cell-type conditional knockout (Pcp2-cre, Emx1-cre) supports a whole-gene claim as strongly as a null, and the Alliance text never says an allele (including Meis1 em1Rihw at H1.1) is a loss of function

one mouse MGI annotation alone makes each human-gene statement (S1, S3, S5, S6, S8) 'established' at belief 4/5, exactly the threshold; the taxon mismatch is flagged (taxonConsistent false) but not discounted

audit.before: MEIS1 →+ circadian sleep/wake cycle (GO:0042745), evidence []; the MGI record excluded as no_direction
audit.after: MEIS1 →− Sleep-wake cycle disturbance (HP:0006979) with a sign_note; the MGI record kept: curatedDb, taxon mouse, quote '... Meis1<em1Rihw>/Meis1<em1Rihw> ... shows abnormal circadian sleep/wake cycle'
audit.reason: The step's object is the *normal* cycle, so 'required for normal X' means that losing MEIS1 gives an abnormal cycle. A cycle has no amount, so this is the guide's undirected change (an effect, +, on the abnormal-X phenotype), inverted for the loss. The record states exactly that, and the run's mechanism quotes it the same way. The curator's own guide problem says this mapping would keep the record. This also matches how the curator treated the same MGI record type at S3, S5, S6 and S8, and how the multi_agent-r2 RLS curation handled the same MEIS1 record. S1 is now established at 4/5, like the others.

audit.before: circadianSleepWake (GO:0042745) →− risk of RLS; sign_note: 'disrupted' read as loss of the normal cycle
audit.after: sleepWakeDisturbance (HP:0006979 'Sleep-wake cycle disturbance') →+ risk of RLS; no inversion; GO:0042745 entity removed
audit.reason: A 'disrupted circadian sleep/wake cycle' (the run gives its kind as phenotype) is an abnormal cycle, not less cycling. The run's mechanism calls it 'an abnormal circadian sleep/wake cycle'. That is the guide's undirected change, and an abnormal-X term exists (HP:0006979, the human match of MP:0020478), so the step is an effect, +, on that term. 'Disrupted' is not in the loss-of-function list; by the curator's own account, they chose that reading because it connected H1. H1 still connects, because H1.1 now ends at the same phenotype. The arm is unchanged: S1 → S2, sign neg, belief 0.

audit.before: target abnNervousElectrophys: HP:0001311 'Abnormal nervous system electrophysiology', with no site
audit.after: target somatosensoryElectrophysAbn: HP:0001311 refined with anatomy somatosensory system (UBERON:0003942)
audit.reason: The step's object is 'abnormal somatosensory-circuit morphology and electrophysiology'. The qualifier covers both parts, and it is the point of H2: the title says 'somatosensory-circuit dysfunction', and the falsification restores BTBD9 'in somatosensory neurons'. The curator kept the qualifier for morphology (MP:0000860) but dropped it for electrophysiology. That fitted the node to the record, not to the step.

audit.before: kept: curatedDb, mouse, quote '... Btbd9<tm1d(EUCOMM)Wtsi>/Btbd9<tm1d(EUCOMM)Wtsi> ... shows abnormal nervous system electrophysiology'
audit.reason: The record is a whole-body tm1d knockout with abnormal nervous-system electrophysiology and no site. It does not state a change in somatosensory circuits. S4 drops from established (4/5) to unsupported. The kept-evidence total stays at 5, because S1 gained one.

audit.before: 'abnormal neural iron homeostasis' merged into abnIronHomeostasis (HP:0011031); H4 route S8 → S9, sign neg
audit.after: neuralIronHomeostasisAbn: HP:0011031 refined with anatomy nervous system (UBERON:0001016); H4 has no route
audit.reason: The run adds 'neural' only at H4.2; H4.1's record is a whole-body Aco1 knockout. The falsification ('perturb ACO1 in an adult neural lineage while controlling systemic iron, then measure brain iron') makes neural versus systemic iron the point of the hypothesis. The curator noted this but merged anyway, so H4 composed across the very gap the run sets out to test (compare the fyttd1-elac2-als-or-plus audit). The arm's belief was 0 either way; claims with no route go from 2 to 3.

audit.after: S10: sleepSensoryDysfunction →+ risk of RLS (PMID:17637780, rs10947738, rs61192259, rs4714163 excluded). S11: sleepSensoryDysfunction →+ Periodic limb movements of sleep, HP:5200295 (PMID:17634447 excluded). sleepSensoryDysfunction is HP:0011730 'Abnormal central sensory function' refined with stage sleep (GO:0030431)
audit.reason: 'Sensory-circuit dysfunction' is an undirected change, and an abnormal-X term exists for it (HP:0011730: 'an abnormality of sensation related to CNS function'). 'Sleep-dependent' is a stage refinement. So the node is broad but not missing, and the step is expressible. The compound object splits into RLS and PLMS; the curator had already found HP:5200295. No citation mentions sensory circuits, so both statements are unsupported and no arm changes. Each citation is listed once, under the part it bears on most, so the exclusion count stays 11.

audit.before: the MGI record 'gives no direction and does not say the allele is a loss of function'
audit.after: removed; the allele caveat moved into the evidence_weighting finding, which now lists H1.1 (Meis1 em1Rihw)
audit.reason: The record now states S1 and is kept. The allele caveat applies equally to the kept BTBD9, PTPRD and ACO1 records.

audit.before: 'sleep-dependent sensory-circuit dysfunction' is too vague to ground
audit.reason: The label is grounded now (S10, S11).

audit.item: findings chain_not_connected (H1, H2, H4), confidence_unjustified (H1, H2), rule_missing (H1.1, H1.2, HP/MP), evidence_weighting (both)
audit.before: details written for the curator's groundings: GO:0042745, the merged iron node, H2.3 unexpressed, S4 kept; the H1 confidence finding said no citation states any of its steps
audit.after: details and step lists updated to the audited curation. H4 is now recorded as having no route; H1.1 is stated by one mouse record; the 'established on one record' statements are S1, S3, S5, S6 and S8
audit.reason: These follow from the changes above.

audit.after: hypothesis-agent contradicting_evidence_ignored: the cited abstract associates the BTBD9 variant with periodic limb movements without RLS, and reports 'the absence of such an association for RLS without periodic limb movements'
audit.reason: The run cites this paper for 'RLS and periodic limb movements' and builds a sensory mechanism, but its own source ties the locus to PLMS rather than to RLS's sensory component. The curator read the text (the exclusion reason mentions PLMS) but drew no finding from it.
